messages:
alex: Hey team — customer (acct: corp-zen) seeing intermittent 502s and spikes in tail latency for /v1/generate since ~09:30 UTC. They gave one request id: r-0a1b2c3d. Also seeing 401s for a small subset right after a token refresh. Can we get a minimal repro and the exact capture steps to send back?

mira: Thanks. Can you ask for the full X-Request-ID response header value and the exact timestamp (client-side) when that r-0a1b2c3d occurred? Also which region (us-east-1 / eu-west-1)?

alex: Sent back to customer: please paste the full response headers and the client request timestamp. region: us-east-1. They returned two headers: \"X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d\" and \"X-Region: us-east-1\". Client timestamp 2026-03-17T09:31:12.341Z.

sam: OK, let me drop a minimal curl + SDK repro. Ask customer to run these from the same machine that triggered the error (helps capture local network/egress).

sam: CURL (swap in API_KEY and REQUEST_TS):
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-4o-mini\",\"input\":\"hi\",\"max_tokens\":16}' \
  \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\" \
  -w \"\\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\\nX-REQUEST-ID:%{header_x-request-id}\\nTOTAL_TIME:%{time_total}\\n\"
```

sam: Python minimal repro (requests, prints headers + timings):
```
import os, time, requests
API_KEY = os.getenv('API_KEY')
url = 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'
payload = {'model':'gpt-4o-mini','input':'smoke','max_tokens':8}
start = time.time()
r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {API_KEY}'}, timeout=30)
print('status', r.status_code)
print('x-request-id', r.headers.get('X-Request-ID'))
print('elapsed', time.time() - start)
print('resp', r.text)
```

sam: JS (node fetch) minimal repro:
```
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
const API_KEY = process.env.API_KEY
const url = 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'
const body = JSON.stringify({model:'gpt-4o-mini', input:'smoke', max_tokens:8})
;(async ()=>{
  const t0 = Date.now()
  const r = await fetch(url, {method:'POST', body, headers:{'Authorization':`Bearer ${API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type':'application/json'}})
  console.log('status', r.status)
  console.log('x-request-id', r.headers.get('x-request-id'))
  console.log('elapsed_ms', Date.now()-t0)
  console.log('text', await r.text())
})()
```

sam: Go minimal repro (net/http):
```
package main
import ("bytes" "fmt" "net/http" "os" "time")
func main(){
  apiKey := os.Getenv("API_KEY")
  url := "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate"
  payload := []byte(`{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"smoke","max_tokens":8}`)
  t0 := time.Now()
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", url, bytes.NewBuffer(payload))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+apiKey)
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  client := &http.Client{Timeout: 30 * time.Second}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err!=nil { fmt.Println("err",err); return }
  fmt.Println("status", resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println("x-request-id", resp.Header.Get("X-Request-ID"))
  fmt.Println("elapsed_ms", time.Since(t0).Milliseconds())
}
```

jordan: Nice. Also ask customer to capture a HAR or tcpdump if they can, and to run the curl with `-v` to capture TLS handshake times. For the 401-after-refresh: have them log the token expiration times and whether they get a 401 immediately after rotating a short-lived refresh.

alex: Customer tried the curl and got 502 twice (HTTP_CODE:502) and x-request-id header present on the second attempt: r-0a1b2c3d. They also say a different request around the same time returned 401 with x-request-id r-9f8e7d6c.

mira: Please ask them to collect the following and upload to support portal: 
- the curl output (with -v) including full response headers, 
- the SDK run outputs (stdout), 
- HAR export (if browser), 
- client-side timestamp mapping to server X-Request-ID, and 
- short note: token refresh timing & method (STS, OIDC, manual). 
Also confirm tenant/account id and whether they recently changed billing/payment method (sometimes billing disables endpoints -> 402/403, but that shouldn't cause 502s).

alex: I asked for those. They uploaded curl output and the python stdout. Curl shows detailed TLS handshake and then: `HTTP/2 502`, response body: `{"error": "backend temporarily unavailable"}`, header `X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d`. Python run showed 401 earlier with `x-request-id: r-9f8e7d6c` and a local token refresh at 09:29:07Z.

mira: Filing a short triage for infra: payloads + both request ids + region + approximate client timestamps. @oncall-bot can you take a look at us-east-1 edge/ingestor logs for r-0a1b2c3d and r-9f8e7d6c? :search: :hourglass_flowing_sand:

oncall-bot: Acknowledged. Routing to eng-runtime oncall. Ticket #INC-2026-041 opened with logs requested.

sam: For the reply to customer, include the minimal SDK snips above, plus a tiny retry wrapper they can copy that retries on 502 with jitter and logs x-request-id each attempt. Example (python):
```
for i in range(3):
  r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=30)
  print('attempt', i, 'status', r.status_code, 'x-request-id', r.headers.get('X-Request-ID'))
  if r.status_code<500: break
  time.sleep(0.2 * (2**i))
```

jordan: Also remind them to mask API keys when sharing and to rotate creds after sending raw logs.

alex: Got it. I'll send the repro snips + upload checklist and link the support ticket. Will update thread when oncall posts logs. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Note: customer corp-zen is on Dedicated contract with invoice status: paid. No billing block detected.

mira: Thanks — this looks good. Closing the loop once oncall attaches the edge traces.
